curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: make predictions about a story using the title and the pictures

mission.title: make predictions about a story using the title and the pictures

interactions.prompt: The title is ‘The Lost Puppy’. What will the story probably be about?
interactions.feedback: Yes! The title gives a strong clue about the story.
interactions.retryHint: Look for the choice that matches the words lost puppy.

interactions.prompt: The cover shows dark clouds and a child holding an umbrella. What may happen next?
interactions.feedback: Correct! Clouds and an umbrella are picture clues for rain.
interactions.retryHint: What weather makes us carry an umbrella?

interactions.prompt: Title: ‘Grandma's Surprise’. The picture shows Grandma hiding a wrapped box. What is a good prediction?
interactions.feedback: Great prediction! Both the title and wrapped box support it.
interactions.retryHint: What is usually inside a wrapped surprise?

interactions.prompt: Title: ‘The Fast Tortoise’. The picture shows a tortoise at a race line. What might the story explore?
interactions.feedback: Well done! Your prediction uses both title and picture.
interactions.retryHint: Find the choice connected to a tortoise at a race.

interactions.prompt: Title: ‘Market Day’. The picture shows an empty basket and a family leaving home. What may happen first?
interactions.feedback: Excellent! The empty basket and title work together as clues.
interactions.retryHint: What do families commonly do with baskets at a market?

interactions.prompt: Which is the best way to make a prediction before reading?
interactions.feedback: You are a prediction explorer! Titles and pictures help us make sensible guesses.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the method that uses all available clues.
